seoTitle: How to Know if Your Shopify Store Is Really Live 2026
metaDescription: Not sure if customers can actually see your Shopify store? Here's how to confirm your store is published, your domain works, and checkout is live.
intro: New Shopify sellers often finish setup and still aren't sure whether anyone else can actually see their store. This guide covers the quick checks that confirm your store is genuinely live: reading the real signals in your admin dashboard, confirming your theme's Live status directly in the theme editor, and then verifying your domain, product visibility, and checkout so nothing blocks a customer who finds you. Running through these before you announce your store means you find gaps before a customer does.

steps.heading: Check your admin Home dashboard for real activity
steps.body: Your Shopify admin Home page shows Sessions, Total sales, Orders, and Conversion rate for a rolling date range, with a chart plotting sessions day by day. Seeing any nonzero session count here — even a small one — is meaningful: it means real visitors are reaching your storefront, which only happens if the store is published and reachable. A flat chart at zero across every day is your first warning sign that something upstream, like password protection or a broken domain, is blocking traffic before it ever counts.

image.caption: The Shopify admin Home dashboard, showing Sessions, Total sales, Orders, and Conversion rate with a day-by-day traffic chart underneath.

steps.heading: Open Online Store > Themes and check your current theme
steps.body: From the left sidebar, go to Sales channels > Online Store > Themes. This page lists your published theme — labeled "Current theme" — along with core performance metrics like LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) and INP (Interaction to Next Paint), both marked "Good" in a healthy store. If you see a theme here at all with a Customize button next to it, that confirms you have an active theme assigned to your storefront rather than an unfinished setup with nothing published.

image.caption: The Themes page under Online Store, showing the current theme (Dawn), its performance scores, and the Customize button that opens the theme editor.

steps.heading: Confirm the Live badge in the theme editor
steps.body: Click Customize on your current theme to open the theme editor, and look at the top-left corner next to the theme name — a green "Live" badge next to "Dawn 15.4.0" (or whatever theme you're running) is the most direct confirmation available that this is the theme customers actually see when they visit your store right now, not a draft or unpublished variant. If that badge instead reads something like "Unpublished" or is missing entirely, customers are not seeing this theme, no matter how finished it looks in the editor.

image.caption: The theme editor for the current theme, with a green "Live" badge next to the theme name — direct confirmation that this is what customers see.

steps.heading: Test your domain from outside your own devices
steps.body: Open your custom domain in a browser on a different device or network than the one you used to build the store — a phone on mobile data works well for this. You're checking that the domain actually resolves to your storefront rather than a Shopify placeholder page, a parking page from your registrar, or nothing at all, which can happen if DNS records haven't fully propagated yet after connecting a domain.

steps.heading: Verify your products are visible, not just created
steps.body: Back in the admin, open Products and check that the items you want customers to buy show an Active status and are assigned to the Online Store sales channel specifically. A product can exist in your catalog and still be invisible to shoppers if it's left in Draft status or was never added to that sales channel — both are common gaps after a bulk import or a rushed initial setup.

steps.heading: Run a test purchase to confirm checkout works
steps.body: Finally, use Shopify's test payment gateway (Settings > Payments) to run a complete purchase through checkout without charging a real card, or place a genuine low-cost order if you'd rather see the full customer experience end to end. This is the check that catches problems the other steps can't — a misconfigured payment provider or a broken checkout step that only shows up when someone actually tries to pay.

faq.question: Why does my Shopify store show a password page to visitors?
faq.answer: Shopify stores start with password protection enabled by default during setup, so if you haven't turned it off in Online Store > Preferences, visitors will hit that page instead of your storefront even if everything else is configured correctly.

faq.question: How do I know if my domain is properly connected?
faq.answer: Open your custom domain in a browser on a device or network you haven't used to edit the store, and confirm it loads your actual storefront rather than an error page or a Shopify placeholder.

faq.question: How can I tell if my theme is actually live?
faq.answer: Open Online Store > Themes and click Customize on your current theme. A green "Live" badge next to the theme name in the top-left corner of the editor confirms customers are seeing that exact theme right now.

faq.question: Can I check if my store is live without making a real purchase?
faq.answer: Yes — Shopify offers a test payment mode in Settings > Payments that lets you run through the entire checkout flow without charging a real card.

faq.question: My products aren't showing up on the storefront — why?
faq.answer: This usually means the product's status is set to Draft or it hasn't been added to the Online Store sales channel, both of which you can fix from the product's page in Products in your admin.
